about: The game's English text (S16, D-game-13): everything a player with no Spanish reads in English. English is on-screen text only; only Spanish is spoken. The core is not changed: the feedback below is keyed by the core's error codes (nlp ErrorTags) and by the outcome of a turn, with a fallback for a code the game does not know. Placeholders: {expected} and {actual} (the core's forms), {npc}, {noun}, {blocks}, {tag}. Edit here, then re-hash the bundle.

ui.retry: Not quite. Try once more, or press H for help.
ui.helpDefault: Listen to the guide again, then say it as shown on the card. You can press K to skip this step.
ui.objectiveFindGuide: Go down the trail and find the guide
ui.objectiveLightFire: Go back up the trail and light your own fire
ui.objectiveComplete: Session complete: your fire is lit
ui.spareTorch: A spare torch is in your bag. Take it up the trail and light your own fire.
ui.sessionCompleteLine: Very good! Now you have a fire.
ui.btnHold: hold to speak; Esc cancels or closes

controls.keys: W A S D or the arrow keys

controls.text: Collect wood from a tree or fruit from a bush (aim the dot in the middle of the screen at it).
Place the item you are holding.
Choose an item in the bar at the bottom.
Talk to someone. T lets you type, V lets you speak.

controls.keys: C, or E at the workbench
controls.text: Make things from what you carry.
Your words and phrases, and how well you know them.

controls.keys: Hold V or Space in a conversation
controls.text: Speak into the microphone. Let go when you are done.

controls.keys: W or Tab in a conversation
controls.text: Type your answer instead. Enter sends it.
Help: shows the English and the phrase to say.
“No sé” means I don't know. It is never wrong.

controls.keys: R and S in a conversation
controls.text: Hear the last line again, or more slowly.

controls.keys: Enter, K, L during a lesson
controls.text: Enter: continue. K: skip this step. L: start the lesson at the guide.
Cancel, or close what is open.

tips.text: Move the mouse to look around. The valley below is where you are headed.
Walk with W A S D. The trail starts beside your camp.
Press Space to jump up a ledge or over a gap.
A note is pinned to your tent: “Welcome, traveller. My camp is down the trail, past the trees. Follow the camino (the trail) and come and say hello. Luna”
Aim the dot in the middle of the screen at a tree trunk and hold the left mouse button to collect wood.
What you collect appears in the bar at the bottom. Press I to see everything you carry.
Press E to talk to someone. The English under the Spanish is there to help you.
Hold V (or Space) to speak, or press W to type. Press H for help any time. Nothing here is a test: if you are not sure, press N for “I don't know”.
The list at the top right shows what the camp needs. The English next to each word goes away once you know the word.

phrases.que-necesitas: The shopkeeper is asking what you need.
phrases.pedir-agua: Use this to ask for something. “Quiero” means I want, and “por favor” means please.
phrases.quieres-pan: The shopkeeper is offering you bread.
phrases.si-por-favor: Say this to accept an offer politely: yes, please.
phrases.no-gracias: Say this to turn an offer down politely: no, thank you.
phrases.donde-esta-el-rio: Use this to ask where something is. “Dónde está” means where is.
phrases.hola: Say this to greet anyone. It means hello.
phrases.gracias: Say this when someone helps you. It means thank you.
phrases.adios: Say this when you leave. It means goodbye.
phrases.no-se: Say this when you do not know what to say. It is never wrong.
phrases.ayuda: Say this to ask for help.
phrases.me-llamo: Luna is telling you her name. “Me llamo” means “my name is”.
phrases.es-madera: Luna is asking whether something is wood. “Es” means “it is”.
phrases.si: Say this to answer yes to a question.
phrases.no: Say this to answer no to a question.
phrases.que-es-esto: Use this to ask what something is. “Qué” means what and “esto” means this.
phrases.quieres-fruta: Luna is offering you some fruit. “Quieres” means “do you want”.
phrases.de-nada: The polite answer to “gracias”. It means you are welcome.
phrases.otra-vez: Use this when you did not catch something. The guide says her last line again.
phrases.mas-despacio: Use this when the guide speaks too fast. She says her last line again, slowly.
phrases.necesitas-madera: Luna is telling you what the camp needs. “Necesitas” means “you need”.

lines.spanish: ¡Hola! Soy la guía. ¿En qué te ayudo?
lines.english: Hello! I am the guide. How can I help you?
See you later. Have a good day!
Are you sure? Say it again.
Say “ayuda” and I will help you.
Hello, friend! What are you looking for?
Good morning. How can I help you?
Hello again. What are you looking for?
Let me see, I will look.
Let me see what it is.
Of course, I will help you!
Let us see if it is that.

lines.spanish: Mira una cosa y dime qué es.
lines.english: Look at something and tell me what it is.

lines.spanish: No sé qué es. Mira algo.
lines.english: I do not know what it is. Look at something.
I do not know what it is.

lines.spanish: Busca una cosa y pregunta otra vez.
Pregunta por una cosa. ¿Dónde está la piedra?
lines.english: Ask about something. Where is the stone?
Let me see, I will tell you.
Let me see, I will search.
You do not need anything else.
Let us see, what is this?

lines.spanish: No te entendí bien. ¿Lo dices otra vez?
lines.english: I did not catch that well. Can you say it again?

lines.spanish: No te entendí bien. ¿Me lo dices otra vez?
lines.english: I did not catch that well. Can you say it to me again?

lines.spanish: No te entendí. ¿Me lo dices otra vez?
lines.english: I did not understand you. Can you say it to me again?

lines.spanish: Toma la botella. El agua está en el río.
lines.english: Here is the bottle. The water is at the river.

lines.spanish: Aquí tienes la botella. El agua está en el río.
lines.english: Here is the bottle. The water is at the river.
You can say: “Quiero agua, por favor” (I want water, please).

lines.spanish: Puedes decir: «Sí, por favor» o «No, gracias».
lines.english: You can say: “Sí, por favor” (yes, please) or “No, gracias” (no, thank you).
Hello! What are you looking for?
You can ask: “¿Dónde está el río?” (Where is the river?).
Of course! I will say it again.
Of course! I will say it more slowly.
Very good! You have a fruit.

lines.spanish: Mira. La madera es para la antorcha.
lines.english: Look. The wood is for the torch.
Very good! Now you have a fire.

outcomes.understood_with_mistake: {npc} understood you, but there was a small mistake. That is fine: keep going.
outcomes.not_understood: {npc} did not understand that. Try again, press H for help, or press W to type.
outcomes.uncertain: I could not hear that clearly. That is the microphone, not your Spanish. Try again, or press W to type.
outcomes.dont_know: That is fine. Not knowing is part of learning. Here is the phrase to say.
outcomes.help: Here is some help. Try the phrase on the card.
outcomes.choice: You picked one of the offered phrases. Next time, try saying it yourself.
outcomes.fail_forward: That is fine. The game carries on: you do not need to say it perfectly to continue.
outcomes.pointed: {npc} points to the {noun}, {blocks} blocks away. Follow the arrow.

errors.vocab.wrong: A different word fits here: “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.vocab.unknown: The game does not know the word “{actual}”. Check the spelling, or try another word.
errors.conj.person: The verb ending must match who is speaking. Say “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.conj.tense: The verb is in a different time (tense). Try “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.conj.irregular: This verb is irregular, so it does not follow the usual pattern. Say “{expected}”, not “{actual}”.
errors.gender.agree: Spanish nouns are masculine or feminine, and the words next to them must match. Say “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.noun.number: One or more than one? The noun and the words next to it must match. Say “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.ser_estar: Spanish has two words for “to be”: ser and estar. Try “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.word_order: The words go in a different order in Spanish. Try “{expected}” instead of “{actual}”.
errors.pron.vowel: A vowel sounded a little different. Spanish vowels are short and clear: a, e, i, o, u.
errors.pron.r: The Spanish “r” is a quick tap of the tongue, not the English “r”.
errors.pron.silent_h: The letter “h” is silent in Spanish. Do not pronounce it.
errors.pron.stress: The stress falls on a different part of the word. Listen again and copy the rhythm.

feedback.unknownError: There was a small mistake in “{actual}”. Listen to the guide's version and try again.
